description: Session 10 golden set for retrieval evaluation. Project descriptions and cross-collection questions, each hand-annotated with the documents that are genuinely relevant. Q1–Q5 are budget-only (graded over data/budgets_sample.json) and keep the original relevant_budget_ids; Q6–Q8 span the multi-index corpus (budgets + transcripts + technical docs) and use relevant_source_ids. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant iff its source_id (budget_id / transcript_id / doc_id) is in the relevant set. The distractors are deliberately cross-sector or cross-collection 'similar but irrelevant' documents — the exact failure modes this session attacks (averaged multi-topic queries, the dominant collection flooding the top-k, lexical identifiers diluted by embeddings). Annotation criterion: a document is relevant when it directly addresses the asked-for functionality/topic, not merely shares sector or vocabulary. Session 11 extends Q1–Q5 with a `ground_truth`: the reference estimate a reviewer would expect for that project description, in engineer-days, naming the functional modules and the historical hours each block derives from. It states only what the estimate SHOULD contain: the distractors and traps stay in each query's `note`, because a reference that also asserts what must be excluded penalises context_recall with claims no retrieved context can support. It is written in the vocabulary the chunk text actually carries (project and component names, hours) rather than in BUD-2024-xxx ids, which the rendered chunk does not contain. It is the reference answer of the RAGAS evaluation (scripts/eval_ragas_s11.py). Q6–Q8 stay retrieval-only on purpose: they are cross-collection QA questions ('what did the client say about…'), not estimation requests, so no reference estimate exists for them.

queries.query: Mobile banking application with OAuth2 authentication, PSD2 open banking compliance, strong customer authentication and a transaction ledger.
queries.ground_truth: Unos 55-60 engineer-days (≈460h a 8h/día). Módulos esperados, tomados del presupuesto histórico de una API de banca móvil con OAuth 2.0 y cumplimiento PSD2: backend de autenticación OAuth 2.0 (120h); conectores de open banking PSD2, que incluyen la autenticación reforzada del cliente (160h); servicio de ledger transaccional (140h); y notificaciones push y email (60h).
queries.note: Fintech auth + payments. Trap: BUD-2024-006 (e-commerce marketplace vendor payouts) is 'payments-like' but irrelevant for a banking auth project.

queries.query: Headless e-commerce storefront with a product catalog, shopping cart checkout and personalized product recommendations.
queries.ground_truth: Unos 55-60 engineer-days (≈460h a 8h/día). Módulos esperados, tomados del presupuesto histórico de una tienda headless: API de catálogo de producto (150h), servicio de carrito y checkout (140h), recomendaciones personalizadas (110h) y storefront PWA (60h).
queries.note: E-commerce storefront/catalog/checkout. Trap: finance payment budgets (BUD-2024-003) and healthcare scheduling are close in topic words but wrong domain.

queries.query: Telemedicine platform for patient appointment scheduling and video consultations with HL7/FHIR integration and clinical records.
queries.ground_truth: Unos 65-70 engineer-days (≈560h a 8h/día). Módulos esperados, tomados del presupuesto histórico de una plataforma de telemedicina: capa de integración FHIR (190h), agenda de citas (150h), sesiones de vídeo de telemedicina (160h) y módulo de consentimiento y auditoría (60h). Los registros clínicos y los paneles del equipo asistencial pueden apoyarse en el presupuesto de monitorización remota de pacientes (150h).
queries.note: Healthcare telemedicine. Trap: BUD-2024-011 (pharmacy inventory) and BUD-2024-012 (clinical trials) share the healthcare sector but cover different functionality.

queries.query: Industrial IoT platform ingesting sensor telemetry for predictive maintenance and real-time equipment monitoring in a factory.
queries.ground_truth: Unos 60-65 engineer-days (≈500h a 8h/día). Módulos esperados, tomados del presupuesto histórico de mantenimiento predictivo industrial: ingesta de telemetría de sensores (170h), modelos de mantenimiento predictivo (200h) e integración con el panel SCADA (130h). El pipeline de datos a escala y la previsión pueden apoyarse en el presupuesto de smart metering (200h y 140h).
queries.note: Industrial telemetry/monitoring. Trap: BUD-2024-014 (warehouse AGV coordination) is industrial but logistics, not telemetry-driven maintenance.

queries.query: Real-time payments gateway with fraud detection, transaction reconciliation and a double-entry ledger.
queries.ground_truth: Unos 70-75 engineer-days (≈600h a 8h/día). Módulos esperados, tomados del presupuesto histórico de una pasarela de pagos: núcleo de la pasarela (220h), detección de fraude en tiempo real (200h), conciliación de liquidaciones (120h) y panel de comercio (60h). El ledger de doble entrada se apoya en el servicio de ledger transaccional del presupuesto de banca móvil (140h).
queries.note: Fintech payments. Trap: BUD-2024-006 (e-commerce vendor payouts) and BUD-2024-007 (grocery delivery payments) are lexically near but wrong domain.

queries.query: What did the client say about the Stripe Connect checkout, and how much did marketplace vendor payouts cost?
queries.note: Cross-collection: a meeting (transcript) + a budget + the payments doc all answer this. Routing should hit transcript + budget (+ technical_doc). Trap: a single budgets index would miss the transcript discussion entirely.

queries.query: How do we integrate predictive maintenance with SAP using IDoc/BAPI, and what was discussed about it?
queries.note: Lexical identifiers (SAP, IDoc, BAPI) the embeddings dilute — hybrid search should lift the exact-match doc/transcript. Routing should span technical_doc + transcript + budget.

queries.query: Reference for OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE and PSD2 strong customer authentication.
queries.note: Documentation-shaped query: should route to technical_doc (and the auth meeting). Trap: budget components mention auth but do not answer a 'how-to/reference' question.
